candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication indication / aprepitant
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize aprepitant as an NK1 receptor antagonist used with other antiemetics to prevent acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting rather than to treat established symptoms.

options.A: Prevent acute and delayed chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting
options.B: Treat nausea and vomiting only after symptoms are already established
options.C: Reduce febrile neutropenia by stimulating neutrophil production

candidate.rationale: Current aprepitant labeling states that aprepitant capsules, in combination with other antiemetic agents, are indicated for prevention of acute and delayed nausea and vomiting associated with highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy and for prevention of nausea and vomiting with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy. The label also states that aprepitant has not been studied for treatment of established nausea and vomiting. It is an NK1 receptor antagonist, not a granulocyte colony-stimulating factor or a mucositis-prevention therapy. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Aprepitant is used with other antiemetics to prevent acute and delayed CINV in specified chemotherapy settings and is not established for treatment of nausea/vomiting after symptoms are already present.
candidate.source_locator: Full Prescribing Information §1.1 Prevention of Chemotherapy Induced Nausea and Vomiting (CINV): in combination with other antiemetic agents, prevention of acute and delayed nausea/vomiting with highly emetogenic chemotherapy and prevention with moderately emetogenic chemotherapy; §1.3 Limitations of Use: not studied for treatment of established nausea and vomiting
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client receiving highly emetogenic cancer chemotherapy is prescribed aprepitant as part of a multidrug antiemetic regimen. What is the purpose of aprepitant in this setting?
